why: The twenty class swaps, the CSS block and the colour mappings are given exactly and the lines hold (product-card 109/110, checkout-form 460, globals.css dark block ending near 169). But the new block sits on every public page at specificity html:not([data-admin]) (0,1,1), above :root, so it silently overrides any owner CSS or outside theme that defines --brand, --card, --line or --ink on :root (custom-css.test.ts already uses `:root { --brand: ... }` as an example); no test or check covers that, and the scan test's import walker is intricate enough to be written wrongly yet pass its four planted cases.
harm_if_wrong: Shops whose own CSS or imported theme uses a variable named --brand, --card, --line or --ink change colour on deploy, and the checkout's address field changes look, without any check failing.
make_it_cheaper: Write the selector as :where(html:not([data-admin])) (specificity 0) so an owner's :root variables still win, and add a unit case that a store's custom CSS --brand survives; then a wrong edit is caught and the step is cheap.
brief_problems: html:not([data-admin]) outranks :root, so the block overrides owners' and outside themes' variables of the same names; the brief does not mention it.
The e2e step on the hosted invoice leaves a choice (which test carries the assertion if none opens the page).
